verdict.rationale: Supabase documents ways to scope what an agent can do. The MCP connection can be limited to one project (`project_ref`), to read-only Postgres access (`read_only`), and to selected tool groups (`features`), and the publishable key reaches only what RLS allows. However, the agent's actual credential (a PAT) cannot be least-privilege yet: the docs say 'for now all scopes are required.' So the scoping comes from connection parameters, not from the credential itself. Missing for 10: fine-grained PAT/credential scopes, per-agent credential issuance and revocation, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: `read_only=true` — Execute all queries as a read-only Postgres user; `project_ref=<id>` — Scope to a specific project (disables account tools); `features=<groups>` — Enable only specific tool groups
you can create a personal access token (PAT) with the necessary scopes and pass it as a header to the MCP server
In the future, the MCP server will support more fine-grained scopes, but for now all scopes are required
Publishable key | Anyone can read it, so it only reaches what Row Level Security allows
